# The crossing to Abyssinia: seven messages for the WhatsApp pilot (experiment X6)
# Draft. Not reviewed. A teacher reads each one before it is sent.

Day 1
The crossing to Abyssinia. Today we stand at Aksum. Makkah is 817 km to the north, in a straight line.

Day 2
The text gives no date for the emigration, so no sky is drawn. Drawing one would need a date the text does not give.

Day 3
A puzzle: the text gives a total of 83 for this list (Men who emigrated to Abyssinia, “if ʿAmmār was among them” (the list also names women)). Three different counts: the total the text states for this list, the names the extraction found in it, and the name records at this event with no side recorded (counted separately, under who was there). Before tomorrow, guess: does the list of names hold more, fewer or exactly 83?

Day 4
Answer: the reading of the list found 87 names. They differ. Scholars keep three things apart: what happened, the text, and our reading of the text.

Day 5
The text names 127 people at this event.

Day 6
Three questions, from memory:
1. From Aksum, which way does Makkah lie?
2. What total does the text state for this list: Men who emigrated to Abyssinia, “if ʿAmmār was among them” (the list also names women)?
